text: MGM Resorts International, a Delaware corporation incorporated in 1986, operates as a holding company and, through its subsidiaries, owns and manages integrated casino, hotel, and entertainment resorts in the United States and Macau. MGM Growth Properties LLC (“MGP”), a consolidated subsidiary of MGM Resorts, is structured as an umbrella partnership REIT (UPREIT), with substantially all of its assets owned by and its businesses conducted through MGM Growth Properties Operating Partnership LP (the “Operating Partnership”). Under a master lease agreement, a subsidiary of MGM Resorts (the “tenant”) leases real estate assets of The Mirage, Mandalay Bay, Luxor, New York-New York, Park MGM (branded as Monte Carlo prior to May 2018), Excalibur, The Park, Gold Strike Tunica, MGM Grand Detroit, Beau Rivage, Borgata, and MGM National Harbor from a subsidiary of the Operating Partnership (the “landlord”). The Company believes it owns or invests in some of the finest casino resorts globally and reinvests in its properties through renovations, new hotel rooms, restaurants, entertainment, and amenities to maintain competitive advantage. In August 2016, the Company acquired Boyd Gaming’s ownership interest in Borgata, which became a consolidated subsidiary, and subsequently MGP acquired Borgata’s real property. In December 2016, MGM National Harbor opened, and in October 2017, MGP acquired the long-term leasehold and real property associated with it. In February 2018, MGM Cotai opened on the Cotai Strip in Macau, and in August 2018, MGM Springfield opened in Springfield, Massachusetts. In July 2018, MGP acquired Northfield Park Associates, LLC (“Northfield”) for approximately $1.1 billion, and simultaneously entered into a management agreement with an affiliate of Hard Rock Café International (STP, Inc.). In September 2018, the Company agreed to acquire all operating assets of Northfield from MGP for approximately $275 million, subject to customary adjustments, with the transaction expected to close in the first half of 2019. In December 2018, the Company entered into a transaction with MGP for approximately $638 million in consideration for renovations to Park MGM and NoMad Las Vegas, with closing expected in the first quarter of 2019, subject to customary conditions. In January 2019, the Company completed the acquisition of Empire City Casino’s race track and casino for approximately $864 million, subject to adjustments, and MGP acquired the real property for approximately $634 million. In connection with this, the Company amended the existing master lease to lease back the real estate assets of Empire City and agreed to provide MGP a right of first offer on undeveloped land adjacent to the property for future gaming facility development. All casino resorts operate 24 hours a day except Empire City, which operates 20 hours a day. The Company’s domestic resorts include Bellagio, MGM Grand Las Vegas (including The Signature), Mandalay Bay (including Delano and Four Seasons), The Mirage, Luxor, New York-New York (including the Park), Excalibur, Park MGM (including NoMad Las Vegas), and Circus Circus Las Vegas on the Las Vegas Strip, and regional operations include MGM Grand Detroit, Beau Rivage, Gold Strike Tunica, Borgata, MGM National Harbor, and MGM Springfield. Over half of the net revenue from domestic resorts comes from non-gaming operations such as hotel, food and beverage, entertainment, and other amenities. The Company markets to diverse customer groups, including convention attendees, and relies on high customer volume to influence room and amenity pricing. Casino operations include slots, table games, and race and sports book wagering, with premium players accessing high-limit rooms and lounges. The Company owns approximately 56% of MGM China Holdings Limited, which owns and operates MGM Macau and MGM Cotai through MGM Grand Paradise, a Macau gaming subconcessionaire whose concession expires in 2020. Macau is the world’s largest gaming destination by revenue, and the Company expects growth in the Asian gaming market to increase visitation at its Macau properties. The Macau government prohibits new concessions or subconcessions but does not limit the number of casinos or gaming areas operated by existing concessionaires or subconcessionaires, though new casinos require government approval. The Company also has business activities through unconsolidated affiliates, including CityCenter Holdings, LLC, which it manages for a fee, and MGP’s Northfield. As of December 31, 2018, the Company’s resort operations included the following guestrooms, casino square footage, slots, and tables: Bellagio (3,933 rooms, 155,000 sq. ft., 1,707 slots, 147 tables), MGM Grand Las Vegas (6,131 rooms, 160,000 sq. ft., 1,570 slots, 127 tables), Mandalay Bay (4,750 rooms, 152,000 sq. ft., 1,213 slots, 71 tables), The Mirage (3,044 rooms, 94,000 sq. ft., 1,189 slots, 82 tables), Luxor (4,397 rooms, 101,000 sq. ft., 1,026 slots, 54 tables), Excalibur (3,981 rooms, 94,000 sq. ft., 1,153 slots, 51 tables), New York-New York (2,024 rooms, 81,000 sq. ft., 1,148 slots, 66 tables), Park MGM (2,898 rooms, 66,000 sq. ft., 842 slots, 56 tables), and Circus Circus Las Vegas (3,764 rooms, 95,000 sq. ft., 1,221 slots, 36 tables), with a subtotal of 34,922 guestrooms, 998,000 sq. ft., 11,069 slots, and 690 tables. Regional operations include MGM Grand Detroit (400 rooms, 127,000 sq. ft., 3,324 slots, 131 tables), Beau Rivage (1,740 rooms, 81,000 sq. ft., 1,784 slots, 81 tables), Gold Strike (1,133 rooms, 48,000 sq. ft., 1,148 slots, 65 tables), Borgata (2,767 rooms, 160,000 sq. ft., 2,825 slots, 183 tables), MGM National Harbor (308 rooms, 146,000 sq. ft., 3,137 slots, 152 tables), and MGM Springfield (252 rooms, 109,000 sq. ft., 2,444 slots, 94 tables), with a subtotal of 6,000 guestrooms (the full number is incomplete in the document). The aggregate market value of the Company’s Common Stock held by non-affiliates as of June 30, 2018, based on the closing price on the New York Stock Exchange Composite Tape, was $15.6 billion. As of February 22, 2019, 536,916,609 shares of the Company’s Common Stock, $0.01 par value, were outstanding.

The total casino square footage across all operations is 48,968, with gaming revenue of $2,541,000, 31,587 rooms, and 2,049 employees. Regional operations include MGM Grand Detroit (Detroit, Michigan) with 400 square feet, $127,000 in revenue, 3,324 table games, and 131 table game positions, where local investors hold approximately 3% ownership; Beau Rivage (Biloxi, Mississippi) with 1,740 square feet, $81,000 revenue, 1,784 table games, and 81 table game positions; Gold Strike (Tunica, Mississippi) with 1,133 square feet, $48,000 revenue, 1,148 table games, and 65 table game positions; Borgata (Atlantic City, New Jersey) with 2,767 square feet, $160,000 revenue, 2,825 table games, and 183 table game positions; MGM National Harbor (Prince George's County, Maryland) with 308 square feet, $146,000 revenue, 3,137 table games, and 152 table game positions, where local investors have a non-voting economic interest; and MGM Springfield (Springfield, Massachusetts) with 252 square feet, $109,000 revenue, 2,444 table games, and 94 table game positions, where a local investor holds a 1% ownership interest. The regional operations subtotal is 6,600 square feet, $671,000 in revenue, 14,662 table games, and 706 table game positions. MGM China operations include MGM Macau – 55.95% owned (Macau S.A.R.) with 585 square feet, $370,000 revenue, 806 table games, and 291 table game positions; MGM Cotai – 55.95% owned (Macau S.A.R.) with 1,362 square feet, $298,000 revenue, 1,218 table games, and 236 table game positions; the MGM China subtotal is 1,947 square feet, $668,000 revenue, 2,024 table games, and 527 table game positions. Other operations include CityCenter – 50% owned (Las Vegas, Nevada) with 5,499 square feet, $139,000 revenue, 1,533 table games, and 126 table game positions, which includes Aria with 4,004 rooms and Vdara with 1,495 condo-hotel units, with the other 50% owned by Infinity World Development Corp.; and Hard Rock Rocksino Northfield Park (Northfield, Ohio) with no square footage, $65,000 revenue, 2,299 table games, and no table game positions, owned by MGP and managed by an affiliate of Hard Rock Café International (STP), Inc. The overall subtotal for other operations is 5,499 square feet, $204,000 revenue, 3,832 table games, and 126 table game positions. The total square footage is 48,968, with total revenue of $2,541,000, 31,587 rooms, and 2,049 table game positions. Casino square footage is approximate and includes gaming floors, race and sports, high limit areas, and casino-specific walkways, excluding casino cage and other non-gaming space. Revenue includes slot machines, video poker machines, and other electronic gaming devices. Table game revenue includes blackjack (“21”), baccarat, craps, roulette, and other table games, excluding poker. Room counts include 1,138 rooms at The Signature at MGM Grand Las Vegas, 1,117 rooms at the Delano and 424 rooms at the Four Seasons Hotel, and 293 rooms at NoMad Las Vegas. The company competes in highly competitive environments with gaming companies, hospitality firms, and non-gaming destinations like Hawaii, facing competition from state-sponsored lotteries, off-track wagering, card parlors, online gambling, and other legalized gaming. Primary competitive methods include locating in desirable markets, maintaining high-quality resorts with luxurious rooms, state-of-the-art convention facilities, and premier dining, entertainment, retail, and amenities; recruiting, training, and retaining qualified employees; offering unique entertainment; and developing distinctive marketing and customer loyalty programs. Customers include premium gaming, leisure and wholesale travel, business travelers, and group customers such as conventions and trade associations. Las Vegas Strip resorts compete with other hotel casinos on or near the Strip, in downtown Las Vegas (about five miles from the center), and elsewhere in the area, with new entrants expanding capacity or building new resorts. Growth in gaming outside Las Vegas increases competition in Las Vegas. Outside Nevada, resorts compete with other hotel casinos in their markets and surrounding regional gaming markets, where location is critical, and also face competition from gaming operations in neighboring jurisdictions and other leisure destinations. In Macau, the three primary customer bases are VIP casino gaming, main floor gaming, and slot machine operations. VIP gaming is sourced externally through gaming promoters who offer credit and complimentary services and are compensated via revenue-sharing and turnover-based commissions; in-house VIP players receive commissions based on rolling chip turnover. Main floor players do not receive commissions, and the profit contribution from this segment exceeds that of VIP due to commission costs. Gaming revenues from main floors have grown significantly and represent the most potential for sustainable growth. To target premium main floor players, premium gaming lounges and stadium-style electronic table games terminals (including table games and slots) have been introduced. VIP gaming uses special purpose nonnegotiable gaming chips to track wagering, with promoter commissions based on a percentage of gross table games win or turnover and a complimentary allowance based on turnover, recorded as a reduction of casino revenue. In-house VIP commissions are based on rolling chip turnover and are also recorded as a reduction of casino revenue. Key competitors in Macau include five other gaming concessionaires and subconcessionaires; additional concessions could increase competition. Competition also comes from major gaming centers in Asia and globally, including Singapore, Korea, Australia, New Zealand, Malaysia, Vietnam, Cambodia, the Philippines, Russia, cruise ships in Asia, and unlicensed gaming operations. Marketing efforts include advertising on radio, television, internet, billboards, newspapers, magazines, direct mail, email, and social media, as well as through regional offices. Direct marketing uses advanced analytics to identify customer preferences and predict behavior. M life Rewards is a tiered loyalty program that offers benefits across resorts in gaming and non-gaming areas, encouraging total spend within the company’s resorts. The Golden Lion Club is offered for gaming-focused customers at MGM China. Loyalty programs are structured by member value and tier level to allow progressive access to services. The company’s strategy includes operational enhancements, financial strength, corporate social responsibility, geographic expansion, and business model innovation. The company is recognized globally for awards, including Four and Five Diamond designations from the American Automobile Association and multiple Four and Five Star designations from Forbes Travel Guide, as well as certifications in Corporate Social Responsibility. Technology is used to maximize revenue, drive operational efficiency, and serve customers effectively, with information technology automating operations, using data and analytics for decision-making, and applying a cloud-first strategy. The eCommerce platform enables guests and business partners to create all-inclusive experiences with real-time recommendations based on preferences. Employees and management are central to success, with heavy investment in recruiting, training, motivation, and retention, supported by programs such as MGM Resorts University and leadership training. Corporate Social Responsibility is linked to long-term sustainability and profitability, guided by core values of integrity, inclusion, teamwork, and excellence. Four strategic pillars include fostering diversity and inclusion, investing in community, caring for one another, and environmental sustainability. The company promotes diversity to attract talent, drive innovation, expand markets, and strengthen community ties. It creates economic opportunity for local residents, supports education and workforce development, engages local businesses, and promotes responsible gaming through tools like GameSense. Employee-driven initiatives include the MGM Resorts Foundation, Employee Volunteer Program, and Corporate Giving Program, with U.S. employees investing over 123,000 hours of volunteer service in 2018 and a 71% participation rate in giving. Environmental sustainability efforts include energy and water conservation, recycling, waste management, sustainable supply chains, and green construction. Several resorts, including Aria, Vdara, Bellagio, Delano, Mandalay Bay, MGM Grand Detroit, and CityCenter (Aria, Vdara, Veer), have earned Green Key certifications, with Aria, Vdara, Bellagio, Delano, Mandalay Bay, and MGM Grand Detroit receiving the highest “Five Green Key” rating. CityCenter is one of the world’s largest private sustainable developments with six LEED® Gold certifications from the U.S. Green Building Council, and MGM National Harbor, The Park, and T-Mobile Arena have also received LEED® Gold certification. At MGM China, efforts in energy efficiency, indoor air quality, and environmental stewardship have led to inclusion in the Hang Seng Corporate Sustainability Benchmark Index and the China Green Building (Macau) Design label for MGM Cotai. The company allocates resources to invest in existing resorts, strategic developments, and debt repayment or capital returns to shareholders. It regularly evaluates expansion and acquisition opportunities in domestic and international markets, including gaming and entertainment facilities in Nevada or outside Nevada, or outside the United States, for sports and interactive, as well as online gaming. It leverages management expertise and well-recognized brands through strategic partnerships and international expansion. In 2018, the company entered into an agreement with GVC Holdings PLC to form Roar Digital LLC, a 50/50 venture with initial $100 million commitments per partner, which will benefit from the economics of existing race and sports books and online gaming operations and have exclusive access to U.S. land-based and online sports betting, online real money and free-to-play casino gaming, major tournaments, online poker, and similar interactive businesses. Operations commence subject to gaming regulatory approvals. The company’s principal intellectual property consists of trademarks for, among others, Bellagio.

The company is exploring opportunities to expand into new markets for sports and interactive, as well as online gaming, both within Nevada, in other U.S. states, and internationally, leveraging its management expertise and well-recognized brands through strategic partnerships and international expansion. During 2018, the company entered into an agreement with GVC Holdings PLC to form Roar Digital LLC, a 50/50 venture that will be capitalized with initial commitments of $100 million from each partner. The venture will benefit from the economics of the company’s existing race and sports books and online gaming operations and will have exclusive access to U.S. land-based and online sports betting, online real money and free-to-play casino gaming, major tournament and online poker, and other similar interactive businesses. Operations will commence only after receiving gaming regulatory approvals. The company’s principal intellectual property includes registered or allowed trademarks for Bellagio, The Mirage, Borgata, Mandalay Bay, MGM, MGM Grand, MGM Resorts International, Luxor, Excalibur, New York-New York, Circus Circus, Beau Rivage, and Empire City, all of which are registered or applied for in various U.S. classes and other foreign jurisdictions. These brand names are considered vital to the business, as they contribute to customer attraction through name recognition, reputation, and image, and the registrations are of perpetual duration as long as they are used and periodically renewed. As of December 31, 2018, the company had approximately 55,000 full-time and 17,000 part-time employees domestically, with about 6,000 and 3,000, respectively, supporting management agreements at CityCenter; it also had approximately 11,000 employees at MGM China. The company had collective bargaining agreements with unions covering about 39,000 employees, with three major agreements in Las Vegas set to expire in the first half of 2019, and negotiations for successor contracts are expected to begin in the first quarter of 2019. New collective bargaining agreements are also planned for MGM National Harbor and MGM Springfield in 2019. As of December 31, 2018, none of MGM China’s employees were unionized, and the resorts were not party to any collective bargaining agreements. In January 2019, the company acquired operations in New York employing approximately 1,000 employees, some of whom are covered by collective bargaining agreements, with negotiations expected in 2019. In July 2018, MGP acquired its property in Northfield, Ohio, which is operated by an affiliate of Hard Rock International (STP), Inc., and MGM expects to acquire these operations in the first half of 2019, subject to customary closing conditions; the Ohio operation has employees covered by collective bargaining agreements, several of which are expected to be renegotiated in 2019. The gaming industry is highly regulated, and the company must maintain licenses and pay gaming taxes to operate. Each casino is subject to extensive regulation under the laws of its jurisdiction, which generally address the responsibility, financial stability, and character of owners, managers, and those with financial interests. Violations in one jurisdiction could lead to disciplinary action in others. Additional regulations cover alcoholic beverages, smoking, employees, currency transactions, taxation, zoning, building codes (including the Americans with Disabilities Act), construction, land use, and marketing, and the company is subject to anti-money laundering and reporting requirements. The company is also subject to federal, state, and local environmental laws, including the Clean Air Act, Clean Water Act, Resource Conservation Recovery Act, Comprehensive Environmental Response, Compensation and Liability Act, and the Oil Pollution Act of 1990, and owners or operators may be held liable for hazardous substances regardless of prior knowledge or responsibility. No adverse issues related to the company’s properties have been identified. The document includes forward-looking statements that involve risks and uncertainties, such as substantial indebtedness, economic conditions, regulatory compliance, competition, lease risks, MGP’s control, restrictions on operations in China, Macau, Hong Kong, and Taiwan, Macau government actions regarding MGM Grand Paradise’s subconcession, reliance on gaming promoters in Macau, tax policy changes, foreign tax credit valuation, weather risks, concentration on the Las Vegas Strip, credit risk, asset impairments, geopolitical events, co-investing risks, development risks, insurance adequacy, brand protection, anti-corruption laws, pending claims, labor agreements, energy price sensitivity, cybersecurity, corporate social responsibility scrutiny, expansion challenges, gaming tax increases, and potential conflicts of interest among directors and officers due to their roles in MGM China. These statements are made as of the date of the report and are not obligations to update, except as required by law.
